events.what: Zelinsky proves new bounds on T(n) and H(n) for a hypothetical odd perfect number in terms of its smallest prime factor
Stone's improved upper bounds for odd perfect numbers depending on the number of distinct prime factors (Integers 24 (2024) #A114)
Mantovanelli claims no odd perfect number has smallest prime divisor q = 5, 7, 11, 13 or 17, via a finite reduction checked by a certificate release; explicitly leaves q = 3 and q >= 19 open
events.credibility_reason: Single-author preprint claiming an unconditional result (e.g. no odd perfect number coprime to 3 with smallest prime 5) far beyond what is known, via a finite certificate reduction of a kind the problem has resisted; no expert uptake, though under three months have passed, too little for not_credible.

events.what: Self-published full nonexistence 'proofs' on academia.edu, ResearchGate, SSRN, Zenodo, and arXiv:2506.01830
events.credibility_reason: Non-reviewed venues, no uptake on a landmark problem, record's searches found no expert engagement; record did not read them in full.

judgement.doubts: The status now rests on a doubtful, unreviewed case claim. If Mantovanelli's preprint draws no uptake or is found to be wrong, the status falls back to progress (Zelinsky/Stone bounds). The record's researcher wrongly said an unreviewed case would be 'claimed' at best (F1); under §4 it is partial. The self-published whole-problem claims are dated only loosely in the record and are set aside.

outcome_prefix: Judged: the status rests on Mantovanelli's unreviewed July 2026 preprint (arXiv:2607.04365), which claims that no odd perfect number has smallest prime divisor 5, 7, 11, 13 or 17. That is a case of the bullet, and the claim is doubtful.

corrections.why: F1: the record says 2607.04365 'claims to close minimal-prime branches q=5,7,11,13,17' and dismisses it because 'it would only be claimed status at best'. Its abstract states an unconditional closure of those branches, which is a case of the existence question. An unreviewed case that is not knocked down counts as partial, and it outranks the Zelinsky and Stone bounds.
other: the event now relied on proves nonexistence in the settled cases, which is the expected answer.
F8: the status must describe its furthest surviving event. That is the case claim, not the Zelinsky bound.
F8: the credit follows the event the status rests on. The record names the single author as Marco Mantovanelli.
F8: the source must match the new event.
other: kept. The certificates are Python verifier scripts (F9: computer-assisted is not AI), and the record found no AI use in any event.
